findings.summary: On desktop the play board is a narrow portrait column with large empty side areas, and the hint card floats detached at the left. The layout is not re-composed for landscape.

The Level Clear card is clipped at the bottom of the 720px viewport mid-entrance, so the Replay and Next buttons are cut off and Map is out of view in this frame. The settled card in state-won is fine.
The onboarding hint card overlaps the falling ember, hiding the world 4 threat.
The cyan alley backdrop inside the board is very low-contrast, and the world 1 scene feels sparse compared with the furnace world.

blockers.summary: The brief's 'Not now - do not build' list names armored bricks, world hazards and boss levels, and the GDD marks them post-mvp. This commit adds all three: BRICKS.armoredHits, HAZARD (danger line, embers, paddle shrink) and BOSS (four bosses), with matching logic in sim.ts, levels.ts and the pixijs renderer. Scope expansion against an explicit prohibition.

GAME-005 and the GDD require World 2/3/4 to need 5/11/18 total stars, with 12 levels in four worlds of three. STARS now has worldGates [0,10,26,44], levelsPerWorld 8 and levels 32, and RAMP was rewritten to 32 entries. This breaks the acceptance criterion and the design's pacing (36 stars, natural stop after World 1).

Unit tests for stars, unlocks and level select were rewritten to the new 32-level and 10/26/44 gates, and a 298-line levels-and-hazards test was added. They now pin the out-of-scope behaviour instead of the design's rules, so passing checks are not evidence of design fidelity.
?level=N opens any level straight into play regardless of save or unlock state, and is not gated behind a dev build. In a shipped build it lets players bypass the star-gate progression.

findings.summary: The 'Sky Marble' wordmark is semi-transparent and brownish over the scene, so contrast is low, and no Play button or other call to action is visible in the frame. The same happens on mobile/persist-after-reload. It looks like a mid-fade, but as captured it is weak.
The course intro card sits over the middle of the track and hides the goal gate and gems ahead in the first moments. The same occurs on mobile/first-session-1s.
The marble reads dark brick-red rather than the brief's bright coral. Its cream swirl band is muted against the sage track, so it is less of the brightest-thing-on-screen than the identity asks.

review.notes: Docs-only commit. Pause-on-hidden-tab: src/scenes/play-scene.ts update() returns at line 178 while state is 'paused' (after hud.step(), which only bumps the data-steps loop counter), so the run clock and simulation do not advance after the tab returns; only #resume() (player input) restarts play. smoke.spec.ts @pause-resume (lines 351-370) asserts this, and the template-owned lifecycle test requires data-steps to resume, so bind.ts rightly stays unchanged. The verify failures are 30s/5s Playwright timeouts with no cause found in the code I read; the developer's account (parallel desktop+mobile 3D runs on a one-worker machine) is consistent with that, and checks.json records smoke passing at one worker, though I did not run the tests myself (read-only). The insecure-requests failure comes from the template adapter loading the Poki SDK over http from localhost, outside game code. Verify will re-judge the timeouts after approval.

sdk-review.notes: The commit changes only docs/development/* and docs/GDD.md; no src, tests or public file changed since 5137eb3, and the sha equals the development commit. I read the source and did not run anything. Pause on a hidden tab holds the run: bind.ts resumes the 'hidden' reason so the loop counter data-steps restarts (as the template lifecycle test requires), but PlayScene.pause() sets state 'paused' and opens the menu, and update() returns early in that state (src/scenes/play-scene.ts:173-178, 472-496), so the run clock and marble stay frozen until the player presses Resume. The @pause-resume smoke test asserts this. The verify failures are all Playwright timeouts (boot, lit scene, lifecycle, responsive, fallback-follows-boot); I found no cause in the code, and checks.json records the same 18 tests passing at --workers=1 behind the network guard. Verify must confirm it again. The insecure-requests failure comes from the template's Poki adapter loading the SDK over http from localhost, outside game code. Minor doc inconsistency: the GDD specifies six courses but courses.ts defines twelve (the GDD lists an optional extra-course-set), and report.json mvp notes say 'Six courses' while known_issues says twelve; reconcile and list the extra content under design_gaps.

blockers.summary: The verification blocker vr-build-asset-resolution is not fixed. The --fibre data-URI SVG contains filter='url%28%23n%29', and the bundle checker reads it as an unresolved local reference '%23n' in the built CSS. The commit leaves this line untouched, so the 'Fix first' item fails again. Move the texture to a real file under public/ or encode the data URI so no url(#...) reference remains.

This iteration was sent back by verify.fail with six blocking defects (vr-gameplay-boot, vr-gameplay-start, vr-gameplay-core-loop, vr-gameplay-pause-resume, vr-gameplay-responsive, vr-platform-fallback). The commit changes only docs/development/*.json and brief.md. There is no change under src/, tests/ or public/, so none of the defects is fixed.

The lifecycle test requires the simulation step counter (data-steps) to stay constant while the tab is hidden. The developer's known_issues says data-steps still advances while the pause menu waits behind a returning tab. This matches the failing pause-resume and core-loop verification checks on desktop and mobile, and the code was not changed. Pause must stop the simulation and resume must continue it.

The gate saw boot and lit-scene smoke tests exceed 30 s on desktop and flake on mobile, and the no-portal-SDK fallback boot fail. Nothing in the commit fixes or explains this. checks.json says smoke passed locally, and the report says the template's insecure-requests test fails when the network is reachable.
report.json was not updated for this iteration. It still says the e2e run did not happen because of the port 4173 conflict, so it does not describe the build at this commit.
A leftover scratch Playwright config is in the tests tree. The developer asked for it to be deleted. The unused template boot-scene at src/game/boot-scene.ts is also still present.

The commit changes no code under src/, tests/e2e/ or public/. The six verify.fail defects (gameplay boot, start, core-loop, pause-resume, responsive, platform fallback) are attributed to verify running desktop and mobile in parallel, and nothing in the repo shows they are resolved. This is unproven until verify passes on this commit.

known_issues says that after a hidden tab becomes visible, the game loop (data-steps) advances again while the run waits behind the pause menu. The brief requires pause to stop the simulation and resume only on player input (GAME-008). The code is unchanged. The lifecycle test only asserts steps resume when the tab is visible, so it does not guard this.

The boot and lit-scene timeouts, and the no-portal-SDK fallback failure, are blamed on the gate's parallelism with no change. The template's insecure-requests test still fails when the network is reachable, because the adapter loads the Poki SDK over http from localhost. This is not fixed.
The unused template BootScene is still present. The report justifies keeping it because the template's sdk-matrix tests import it. The scratch config tests/zz-alt-port.config.mjs is deleted.

The commit changes only docs/development/*. No code in src/, tests/e2e/ or public/ changed, so the six verify.fail defects (boot, start, core-loop, pause-resume, responsive, platform fallback) are neither fixed nor shown to pass. The blocker from the previous review stands.

bind.ts is unchanged. The developer's own known_issues says the game loop (data-steps) advances again after a hidden tab becomes visible while the run waits behind the pause menu. GAME-008 requires that pause stops the simulation and that resume happens only on player input. The lifecycle test does not guard this.

The smoke test is unchanged. The boot and lit-scene timeouts and the no-portal-SDK fallback failure are still blamed on parallelism without a fix. The template's insecure-requests test still fails because the adapter loads the Poki SDK over http from localhost.
